root_cause: Console.print() with no positional objects always substituted objects=(NewLine(),), ignoring a custom end. So console.print(end="!") printed "\n" instead of "!". In _collect_renderables, `end` is only emitted when it is attached to a joined Text renderable (check_text builds Text(sep, end=end)), so an empty objects tuple renders nothing and a NewLine renderable never carries end.
best_solution: In Console.print, change the empty-objects default: if not objects: objects = (NewLine(),) if end == "\n" else ("",). The empty string goes through render_str into the text list, check_text joins it with Text(sep, end=end), and the output is exactly `end` ("!"). Keeping NewLine() for the default end preserves the existing print() -> "\n" behaviour. The rest of the gold diff is cosmetic: it moves `from os import PathLike` into sorted order and reformats the save_text signature. The PR's 'drop Python 3.8' part lives in pyproject/README, is not in the gold source patch and is not tested.
acceptable_alternatives:
Any change that makes a no-object print emit exactly `end` and leaves print() == "
" and print("foo") == "foo
" unchanged would pass. Examples: objects = (Text(""),) when end != "
", or writing `end` directly when there are no objects. Leaving objects empty does not work, because nothing renders and end is dropped. Appending end unconditionally in _collect_renderables does not work either, because it doubles end on every print.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_console.py::test_print_empty_with_end: Console(file=io.StringIO(), color_system="truecolor").print(end="!") must leave file.getvalue() == "!" exactly (no newline). The existing tests test_print ("foo\n"), test_print_multiple ("foo bar\n") and the markup/style print tests must still pass.
locating_signals: The title 'empty with end' names Console.print's `end` kwarg and the empty-objects branch (`if not objects: objects = (NewLine(),)`), but no function is named. The linked issue #3740 is a red herring: it is a Python 3.14 test_assemble_meta failure for Fedora, unrelated to print. The 'Drop support for Python 3.8' bullet is a chore that pulls agents toward pyproject/README edits.
our_outcome_summary:
All four configs failed in the Kaggle env (v4/v6/v7/v8 = false). v4 (93s, 79 calls) only did the Python 3.8 drop in README.md, README.es.md, docs and pyproject.toml, never touched console.py, and still printed "
". v6 (86s) found the right branch (`if not objects and end == "
"`) but left objects empty, so the output was ''. It also deleted the `if soft_wrap is None:` line, which silently moved `soft_wrap = self.soft_wrap` inside the if. v7 (261s) appended Text(end) unconditionally in _collect_renderables after check_text. That doubled end on every print ('foo


') and broke ~7+ existing tests, and it gave '
!
' for the target. v8 (300s) found the right condition but set objects = () in the elif, so the output was '' (end is dropped when nothing renders); it also committed a stray test_fix.py. The right location was found 2 of 4 times, but no run checked the actual output of console.print(end="!") against "!".
generalizable_lesson: When a PR-description statement mixes a terse behaviour title with an unrelated chore (version drop, docs) and a link that may be irrelevant, the hidden test targets the behaviour in the title: fix source code, not the chore. When a kwarg such as end/sep/suffix is 'ignored in the empty case', trace where the kwarg is actually consumed downstream before choosing the empty-case value. Here it only attaches to a rendered item, so an empty placeholder item is needed, not an empty collection. Always write the one-line repro implied by the title (call with no args plus the kwarg, assert the exact output string), then rerun the existing test module to catch regressions such as doubled output on the common path.
